claims.claim_text: The indexed Negley C. Monett is probably the San Francisco newspaper employee listed in the 1938 and 1941 city directories.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Negley C ... with S F News
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Two contemporary directories repeat the rare exact name and the same newspaper affiliation three years apart.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable. The rare exact name and consistent San Francisco newspaper chronology form a good but not conclusive bridge to the indexed CAF-7 person.
claims.temporal_assessment: The directories establish employment in 1938 and 1941 but do not explicitly connect the job to OSS entry.
claims.match_notes: Box 532 remains necessary to confirm the identity and the sequence into OSS.

claims.claim_text: Negley C. Monett probably worked for the San Francisco News in 1938 and 1941.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Negley C (Elsie G) with S F News
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The 1938 directory says Monett was employed by the newspaper; the 1941 directory says he remained with it.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable identity based on the rare exact name and repeated contemporary employment context.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment, but not proven to be the immediate pre-OSS affiliation or last civilian employer before service.
claims.match_notes: The profile must retain the qualification and must not imply that the newspaper immediately preceded OSS service.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Major John J. Monigan is a high-confidence match to John J. Monigan Jr., the major documented by Harvard's Nuremberg archive.
claims.evidence_excerpt: John J., Jr. Monigan (Major, interrogator, war crimes staff)
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Harvard's authority record supplies the same rare full name and major rank, plus birth, education, and wartime assignment details.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence because the rare full name and major rank agree, with the institutional record adding a compatible suffix and detailed wartime context.
claims.temporal_assessment: Wartime identity evidence only. The authority-record occupation field is not sufficient to date a legal employer or prove a pre-OSS job.
claims.match_notes: The Jr. suffix is preserved as a variant. No law firm is inferred from postwar court materials.
